Sebastião José de Carvalho e Melo, the Marquis of Pombal, was chief minister of Portugal from 1750 to 1777 and its ruler in all but name.

After the earthquake of 1755 he took charge, burying the dead and rebuilding the centre of Lisbon on a grid of straight streets with buildings designed to resist earthquakes. He ruled as an enlightened despot: he expelled the Jesuits in 1759, crushed noble rivals in the Távora affair, ended the legal difference between Old and New Christians and banned bringing slaves into mainland Portugal.

He set up trading companies and fixed the boundaries of the port wine region in 1756. He reformed the University of Coimbra. When King Joseph died in 1777 he was dismissed and put on trial. His reforms were part of the Enlightenment. See Portugal.
sum: Sebastião José de Carvalho e Melo, the Marquis of Pombal, was chief minister of Portugal from 1750 to 1777 and its ruler in all but name.
